claims.content: Customer manages their account settings by updating and saving their membership account information (e.g., first/last name, member ID, email address, phone, password) and managing email notification preferences.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer manages their account settings by updating and saving their membership account information (e.g., first/last name, member ID, email address, phone, password) and managing email notification preferences.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A Customer updates their membership account information on the Manage Account Settings screen and saves the changes successfully.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer is on the Manage Account Settings screen with their membership account information available to edit.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has entered and saved the updated membership account information.
in_scope_actions: Enter updated membership account information (e.g., first/last name, member ID, email address, phone, password)
Change email notification preferences as part of account settings
excluded_adjacent_actions: Manage global/site-wide auction system default settings (Auction Administration)
Downstream administrative processes triggered by saved account settings
variant_dimensions: Which account field is edited (name, member ID, email, phone, password)
Whether the change is to contact information or email notification preferences

claims.content: Customer
The Customer must be authenticated (logged in) to the system, as evidenced by a personalized welcome message.
The Customer must have an existing membership account with registration information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail Address, Phone) and a current password already stored in the system.

missing_aspects: The claim states that prior data 'must be available to populate the account settings fields.' While EC-PC-000 confirms auto-population on the Registration Page 2 mockup, the cited evidence for the Edit pages (EC-PC-002, source pages 51-53) describes displaying information but does not explicitly state or show that these fields are pre-populated for editing in the same manner. The requirement for pre-population on the specific Edit page is not fully supported by the provided cards.

claims.content: The use case is triggered when the Customer accesses the 'My Account Edit Page' (specifically pages for editing Membership Information, Billing/Shipping Addresses, or Payment Methods) to update their stored account data.
The Customer views the 'My Current Information' section, which displays their existing First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address, and Phone.
The Customer enters the Current Password in the 'My Current Information' section to authorize changes.

The Customer enters updated information into the 'My New Information' section fields: First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address (entered twice for verification), Phone, and Password (entered twice for verification).
The Customer checks the email notification preference boxes: 'notify me via email when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', and 'notify me when my winnings are shipped'.
The Customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to submit the updates.
Upon saving changes, the Customer is returned to the My Account page.
The Customer may opt out of the 'Auction Insider' newsletter subscription by clicking the 'Change my "Auction Insider" Email Newsletter Subscription' link.

At main_flow step 2, if the Customer does not complete the current-password authorization required before making any other changes, the system prevents modification of membership account information; the update path is blocked and no account changes can be made.
At main_flow step 5, if the Customer attempts to save a Member ID ('Handle') that is not unique in the database customer table, the system enters an error state.
At main_flow step 5, if the Customer attempts to save an email address that duplicates an existing email in the customer table, the system treats it as an error condition requiring correction.
At main_flow step 5, if the Customer's new password is outside the required 8-to-12 character range, the system triggers a validation error.
At main_flow step 4, if the Customer's payment type is PayPal or Amazon, the 'notify me when I win an auction' email preference checkbox is grayed out, so the Customer cannot de-select it.

missing_aspects: Incorrect current password (wrong value) handling is not specified in the evidence; only incomplete current-password authorization is covered.
Recovery path after rejected save or validation failure (e.g., return to edit fields, retry save, or termination) is not documented in the evidence.
Explicit confirmation that the system 'does not accept' the ID (refusal action).
Explicit confirmation that the system 'does not accept' the email (refusal action).
Explicit confirmation that the system 'prevents the save'.

claims.content: The Customer's updated membership account information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail Address, Phone, Password) is saved to the system and persisted.

The Customer's selected email notification preferences ('notify me when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', 'notify me when my winnings are shipped') are saved and will govern future transactional email behavior.
After saving changes, the Customer is returned to the My Account page.
